mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates an accommodative monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or the average 20-day return in periods with FEDFUNDS < 5.0% is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.3 percentage points over three months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes corporate earnings declines and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return in periods where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp over 3 months is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) and rising interest rates (FEDFUNDS increases > 0.1pp over 3 months) indicates an aggressive monetary tightening cycle that typically leads to reduced corporate profitability and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 2.5% and FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1pp in 3 months
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return in periods meeting the trigger condition is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening demand for residential construction, which typically precedes a broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion periods, the average 20-day forward return following a decline in HOUST is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS) indicates robust consumer spending and corporate hiring, which typically translates to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or the average 5-day forward return in periods of high PAYEMS growth (top 20%) is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 110.0 (index 2017=100) indicates a contraction in manufacturing output, which typically precedes a recession and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 60-day forward return in periods with INDPRO < 110.0 is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Weak retail sales (RSAFS < 370000.0) combined with a restrictive monetary policy (FEDFUNDS > 5.0%) signals a dual threat of slowing consumer demand and tight credit conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: demand contraction with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return in periods meeting the trigger condition is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), a higher level of the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals an accelerating inflation trend that typically triggers aggressive monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), the average 60-day forward return is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
